layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Segmenters for Thin-Structure and Cross-Domain

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Foundation segmentation models such as the Segment Anything Model (SAM) exhibit strong zero-shot

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: generalization through large-scale pretraining, but adapting them to domain-specific semantic segmen-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tation remains challenging, particularly for thin structures (e.g., retinal vessels) and noisy modalities

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: (e.g., SAR imagery). Full fine-tuning is computationally expensive and risks catastrophic forgetting.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: We propose TopoLoRA-SAM, a topology-aware and parameter-efficient adaptation framework for bi-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: nary semantic segmentation. TopoLoRA-SAM injects Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) into the frozen

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ViT encoder, augmented with a lightweight spatial convolutional adapter and optional topology-aware

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: supervision via differentiable clDice. We evaluate our approach on five benchmarks spanning retinal ves-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: sel segmentation (DRIVE, STARE, CHASE DB1), polyp segmentation (Kvasir-SEG), and SAR sea/-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: land segmentation (SL-SSDD), comparing against U-Net, DeepLabV3+, SegFormer, and Mask2Former.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: TopoLoRA-SAM achieves the best retina-average Dice and the best overall average Dice across datasets,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: while training only 5.2% of model parameters (~4.9M). On the challenging CHASE DB1 dataset, our

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: method substantially improves segmentation accuracy and robustness, demonstrating that topology-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: aware parameter-efficient adaptation can match or exceed fully fine-tuned specialist models. Code is

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: available at : https://github.com/salimkhazem/Seglab.git

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Keywords: semantic segmentation , parameter-efficient fine-tuning , topology-aware loss , Segment

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 1 Introduction

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Semantic segmentation underpins numerous critical applications in medical imaging and remote sensing,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: from automated diabetic retinopathy screening [1] to maritime surveillance and environmental monitoring [2]

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: While recent foundation models such as the Segment Anything Model (SAM) [3] have achieved remarkable

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: zero-shot generalization through web-scale pretraining, significant challenges remain when adapting these

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: models to specialized domains with distinct visual characteristics. Two challenges are particularly acute in

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: this setting. First, thin and elongated structures such as retinal vasculature or road networks exhibit extreme

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: aspect ratios, where small pixel-level errors can disconnect entire branches; standard region-based losses (e.g.,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Dice, cross-entropy) are largely insensitive to such topological violations [4, 5]. Second, cross-domain visual

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: shift arises in modalities such as SAR or fundoscopy, whose texture, noise characteristics, and semantics

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: differ substantially from natural images, limiting the transferability of web-pretrained representations [6].

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Full fine-tuning of billion-parameter foundation models is computationally prohibitive and risks catastrophic

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: forgetting of generalizable representations [7]. Parameter-efficient fine-tuning (PEFT) methods such as

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: LoRA [7], adapters [8, 9], and visual prompt tuning [10] offer compelling alternatives by updating only

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: a small fraction of parameters while preserving pretrained knowledge. Recent work has begun exploring

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: PEFT for SAM adaptation [11, 12, 13], yet systematic studies investigating topology-aware adaptation for

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: domain-specific binary segmentation remain limited.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Figure 1 TopoLoRA-SAM architecture overview. We freeze the SAM ViT-B image encoder and inject LoRA mod-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ules (red) into the feed-forward network (FFN) layers of each transformer block. A lightweight depthwise-separable

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: convolutional adapter (green) refines the high-resolution embedding tensor before mask decoding. Training uses a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: topology-aware loss combining BCE, Dice, and clDice.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: In this work, we introduce TopoLoRA-SAM, a principled framework that unifies parameter-efficient adap-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tation with topology-preserving supervision for binary semantic segmentation across diverse domains. Our

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: approach freezes the SAM ViT-B image encoder and injects trainable LoRA modules into its feed-forward lay-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ers, complemented by a lightweight depthwise-separable convolutional adapter operating on high-resolution

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: feature maps. This design enables fine-grained adaptation while preserving the generalizable representations

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: learned during pretraining. To address topological integrity critical for thin structures we incorporate the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: differentiable clDice loss [4], which explicitly optimizes skeleton overlap and encourages connected center-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: lines. Our contributions are: (i) a topology-aware, parameter-efficient adaptation of SAM combining LoRA

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and a lightweight spatial adapter; (ii) a benchmark across five binary segmentation datasets (retinal vessels

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: polyps, SAR sea/land) with region, boundary, topology, and calibration metrics; and (iii) strong performance

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: on CHASE_DB1 and best retina-average Dice while training only 5.2% of model parameters, with a fully

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: reproducible codebase. In this work, ideas related to simplified geometric representations for efficient visual

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: learning [14] and lightweight adaptation via visual prompting [15] are leveraged within a foundation-model

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: segmentation framework.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 2 Related Work

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Semantic segmentation architectures. Fully convolutional networks revolutionized semantic segmentation,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: with U-Net [16] establishing the encoder-decoder paradigm with skip connections that remains foundational

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: in medical imaging. DeepLabV3+ [17| introduced atrous spatial pyramid pooling for multi-scale context

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: aggregation, while recent self-configuring approaches like nnU-Net [18| achieve strong performance through

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: systematic hyperparameter optimization. [19, 20] used these kind of architectures for different applications.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Transformer-based architectures have emerged as powerful alternatives: SegFormer [21] proposes an efficient

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: hierarchical design with lightweight MLP decoders, while Mask2Former [22]| unifies instance, semantic, and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: panoptic segmentation through masked attention. These architectures build upon foundational work on

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: vision transformers [23] and hierarchical designs [24].

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Foundation models for segmentation. The Segment Anything Model [3] represents a paradigm shift,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: trained on over 1 billion masks to enable promptable zero-shot segmentation. While SAM excels at inter-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: active mask generation, adapting it to semantic segmentation particularly for domain-specific binary masks

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: without prompts requires careful consideration of the prompt-mask relationship. SAM 2 [25] extends this

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: capability to video, demonstrating the scalability of the prompting paradigm. However, for domains with

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: significant distribution shift (medical imaging, remote sensing), prompt-free adaptation with task-specific

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tuning remains essential [26].

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: SAM adaptation for specialized domains. Several concurrent works address SAM adaptation for medical

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: imaging. MedSAM [12] fine-tunes SAM on large-scale medical datasets, demonstrating strong generalization

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: across modalities. SAM-Adapter [11] proposes domain-specific adapter modules for underperformed scenes,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: while SAM-Med2D [27] focuses on 2D medical image segmentation. HQ-SAM [28] introduces a high-quality

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: output token for improved mask boundaries. PerSAM [29] enables one-shot personalization through training-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: free prompt learning. Our work differs by jointly addressing parameter efficiency (LoRA + adapters) and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: topology preservation (clDice) for thin-structure domains where connectivity is critical.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Parameter-efficient fine-tuning. PEFT methods enable foundation model adaptation with minimal pa-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: rameter overhead. LoRA [7] reparameterizes weight updates as low-rank matrices, achieving comparable

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: performance to full fine-tuning on language models. AdaLoRA [30] extends this with adaptive rank allo-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: cation, while DoRA [31] decomposes weights into magnitude and direction for improved learning dynamics.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Adapter modules [8] insert trainable bottleneck layers between transformer blocks, and AdaptFormer [9]

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: adapts this for vision. Visual Prompt Tuning (VPT) [10] prepends learnable tokens to input sequences.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Scale-and-shift tuning (SSF) [32] offers an even more parameter-efficient alternative. These methods share

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: the goal of preserving pretrained knowledge while enabling task-specific adaptation.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Topology-aware losses and metrics. Standard overlap metrics (Dice [33], IoU) are insensitive to topological

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: errors that break connectivity in thin structures. clDice [4] addresses this by computing skeleton overlap using

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: differentiable soft-skeletonization, encouraging connected centerlines in tubular structures. Complementary

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: approaches include TopoLoss [5], which uses persistent homology to penalize Betti number mismatches, and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Betti matching [34], which aligns persistence barcodes for topologically faithful predictions. Boundary focused

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: metrics such as BFScore [35] evaluate contour precision. For probabilistic outputs, calibration metrics like

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Expected Calibration Error (ECE) [36, 37] assess reliability, which is critical for clinical deployment [38].

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Recent work emphasizes the importance of comprehensive metric evaluation [39].

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 2.1 Problem Formulation

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Given an input image

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: , we aim to predict a binary semantic mask

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: indicating

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: foreground probability (vessel, polyp, or sea regions). Unlike SAM's promptable paradigm that produces

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: instance-agnostic masks conditioned on user-provided points or boxes, our task requires semantic predictions

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: without runtime prompts. This necessitates adapting SAM's encoder-decoder architecture to directly output

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: semantic masks through end-to-end training.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 2.2 SAM Architecture and Prompt-Free Decoding

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: We adopt the SAM ViT-B architecture [3], comprising: (i) a Vision Transformer (ViT) image encoder with 12

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: transformer blocks, producing embeddings

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ; (ii) a prompt encoder mapping user interactions

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: to embedding space; and (iii) a lightweight mask decoder that combines image and prompt embeddings

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: via cross-attention. For semantic segmentation, we operate in prompt-free mode by providing null prompt

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: embeddings (∅), treating the mask decoder as a semantic prediction head. The decoder outputs a single

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: binary mask, upsampled to the target resolution via bilinear interpolation.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.text: To enable efficient adaptation while preserving pretrained representations, we inject LoRA modules [7] into the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 2.4 Spatial Convolutional Adapter

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: While LoRA enables semantic adaptation of the encoder's representational capacity, thin structures require

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: fine-grained spatial reasoning at higher resolutions than SAM's 16× downsampled embeddings. We introduce

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: a lightweight depthwise-separable convolutional adapter applied to the image embedding tensor z:

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: The adapter comprises a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: depthwise convolution (256 groups) followed by ReLU activation and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: pointwise projection, wrapped in a residual connection. This adds only ~66K parameters while enabling

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: local spatial refinement crucial for thin-structure boundary preservation.

layout_dets.text: 2.6 Implementation Details

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: We use SAM ViT-B pretrained weights and freeze all encoder parameters except LoRA modules. The mask

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: decoder remains trainable (~2.4M parameters). Total trainable parameters: ~4.9M (LoRA: 2.4M, adapter:

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 66K, decoder: 2.4M), compared to 93.7M total. Table 1 summarizes parameter efficiency. Training uses

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: , cosine decay, and 50 epochs

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 3 Experimental Setup

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 3.1 Datasets

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: We evaluate on five binary segmentation benchmarks spanning three distinct application domains:

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Retinal vessel segmentation. DRIVE [1] contains 40 color fundus images (584×565) with manual vessel

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: annotations from expert ophthalmologists, split into 20 train and 20 test images. STARE [40] provides

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 20 images (700×605) with vessels and pathological abnormalities. CHASE_DB1 [41] comprises 28 high-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: resolution images (999×960) from a pediatric population study. These datasets exemplify thin-structure

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: segmentation where topological connectivity is clinically significant for vascular analysis.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Polyp segmentation. Kvasir-SEG [42] contains 1,000 colonoscopy images with corresponding polyp masks,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: representing an important task for early colorectal cancer detection. Images vary in resolution and polyp

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: appearance.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: SAR sea/land segmentation. SL-SSDD [2] provides synthetic aperture radar (SAR) imagery for maritime

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: boundary delineation, challenging due to speckle noise, low contrast, and significant distribution shift from

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: natural images.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 3.2 Preprocessing and Augmentations

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: All datasets are standardized to RGB format with ImageNet normalization

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: [0.229, 0.224, 0.225]). We use dataset-specific resolutions: 384×384 for retinal datasets, 512×512 for Kvasir-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: SEG and SL-SSDD. Training augmentations include random horizontal/vertical flips, random scaling (0.5–

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 1.5×), and center crops with reflection padding. Color jitter is disabled for SAR imagery to preserve modality-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: specific characteristics.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 3.3 Baseline Architectures

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: We compare five segmentation model families spanning convolutional, transformer-based, and foundation-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: model paradigms. As convolutional baselines, we use U-Net [16] with a ResNet34 [43] encoder and DeepLabV3+ [17

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: with a ResNet50 encoder. For transformer-based segmentation, we evaluate SegFormer (MiT-B0) [21] and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Mask2Former [22] with a Swin-T backbone [24]. Finally, we include our TopoLoRA-SAM model, which

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: adapts SAM ViT-B [3] using Low-Rank Adaptation, a lightweight spatial adapter, and optional topology-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: aware clDice regularization. All models use ImageNet-pretrained backbones (or SAM-pretrained weights)

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and are trained with an identical BCE+Dice objective to ensure fair comparison.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 3.4 Training Configuration

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: All experiments follow a unified training protocol. We use the AdamW optimizer with

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and a weight decay of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: . The learning rate is set to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and scheduled using cosine annealing down to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: a minimum value of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: . All models are trained for 50 epochs. A batch size of 4 is used for all baseline

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: models, while SAM-based models are trained with a batch size of 1 and gradient accumulation over 4 steps to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: maintain a comparable effective batch size. Training is performed using mixed-precision (FP16) via PyTorch

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Automatic Mixed Precision (AMP). For robustness, all reported results are averaged over three random seeds

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: (0, 1, and 2), and we report the mean and standard deviation.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 3.5 Evaluation Metrics

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: We use a comprehensive evaluation suite covering region overlap, boundary accuracy, topology preservation,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and calibration. Region-level performance is measured using the Dice coefficient (F1-score) and Intersection-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: over-Union(IoU), with precision and recall reported to characterize false positive and false negative behavior.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Boundary quality is evaluated using the BFScore [35], which computes an F1-score on contour pixels within

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: a tolerance margin. To assess topology preservation for thin structures, we report centerline Dice (clDice) [4]

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: on retinal datasets, capturing connectivity via skeleton overlap. Finally, probabilistic calibration is measured

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: using Expected Calibration Error (ECE) [36], which quantifies the alignment between prediction confidence

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and empirical accuracy; lower values indicate better-calibrated models, an important consideration for clinical

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: decision support.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 3.6 Computational Resources

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: All experiments run on a single NVIDIA RTX A6000 ada (50GB) GPU per training job, with multi-GPU

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: parallelism used only to run independent experiments concurrently. The complete benchmark (5 datasets

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: × 5 models × 3 seeds + ablations + cross-dataset) requires approximately 29.7 GPU-hours, dominated by

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Mask2Former and SAM runs due to larger memory footprint and longer convergence.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 4 Results

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 4.1 Main Benchmark Results

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Table 2 reports Dice scores across all datasets and model families. Overall, TopoLoRA-SAM achieves the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: best average Dice (0.735), outperforming the second-best Mask2Former (0.709) while training only 4.9M

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: parameters, compared to 47.4M for Mask2Former. This highlights the effectiveness of parameter-efficient

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: adaptation of SAM representations.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: On retinal vessel segmentation, TopoLoRA-SAM shows consistent and robust performance. It achieves the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: best Dice on CHASE_DB1 (0.569) with substantially lower variance across seeds, corresponding to a +8.4

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Dice improvement over Mask2Former. On DRIVE and STARE, TopoLoRA-SAM remains competitive with

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: transformer-based baselines and achieves the best retina-average Dice (0.595), indicating stable generaliza-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tion across datasets with different image characteristics.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Across non-retinal domains, TopoLoRA-SAM maintains strong cross-domain behavior, achieving competitive

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Dice on Kvasir-SEG (0.900) and matching state-of-the-art performance on SL-SSDD (0.993), despite the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: significant distribution shift from natural images. These results suggest that SAM representations adapted

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: via LoRA transfer effectively across heterogeneous imaging modalities.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 4.2 Topology Preservation

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: For thin-structure segmentation, region overlap metrics alone are insufficient, as topological connectivity is

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: critical for downstream analysis. Figure 2 summarizes clDice and BFScore on retinal datasets. TopoLoRA-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: SAM achieves the best cIDice on DRIVE (0.678) and CHASE_DB1 (0.599), indicating improved preser-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: vation of vessel connectivity, particularly on high-resolution images where baseline methods often produce

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: fragmented predictions. Improvements are most pronounced on CHASE DB1, with a gain of over 6 clDice

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: points compared to the second-best method.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Boundary quality follows a similar trend. TopoLoRA-SAM achieves the best retina-average BFScore (0.578),

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: with strong gains on CHASE_DB1, highlighting its ability to delineate thin vessel boundaries accurately an

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: important property for vessel diameter estimation and stenosis analysis.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 4.3 Parameter Efficiency Analysis

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Fig 4 visualizes the fundamental trade-off between model capacity and performance on retinal datasets. Key

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: observations:

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: • TopoLoRA-SAM achieves Pareto-optimal performance, offering the best Dice among methods with

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: <10M trainable parameters.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: • Compared to fully-tuned Mask2Former (47.4M params), TopoLoRA-SAM (4.9M params) achieves su-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: perior retina-average Dice with 90% parameter reduction.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: • The lightweight SegFormer (3.7M) shows the lowest parameter count but significantly underperforms

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: on thin-structure preservation.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: This analysis demonstrates that parameter-efficient adaptation of SAM's powerful pretrained representations

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: is a compelling alternative to training specialist segmentation architectures from scratch.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 4.4 Calibration Analysis

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Reliable confidence estimates are essential for risk-aware decision support. Across all datasets, TopoLoRA-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: SAM demonstrates strong calibration, achieving the lowest Expected Calibration Error (ECE) on CHASE_-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: DB1 (0.045) and SL-SSDD (0.003), highlighting its robustness in both medical imaging and remote sensing

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: scenarios. While SegFormer attains the best average ECE overall, this comes at the expense of reduced

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: segmentation accuracy. In contrast, Mask2Former exhibits pronounced miscalibration on CHASE DB1,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: consistent with its high Dice score variability. Overall, TopoLoRA-SAM offers a favorable balance between

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: segmentation accuracy and probabilistic calibration.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 4.5 Component Contributions

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: LoRA adaptation is the primary driver. Adding LoRA modules to the frozen encoder provides the largest

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: single improvement across all metrics: +4.2 Dice, +5.1 clDice, and +8.3 BFScore points over decoder-only

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tuning. This confirms that adapting the encoder's feature representations is critical for domain-specific

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: segmentation, even with a small parameter budget (2.4M additional parameters).

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Spatial adapter provides boundary refinement. The depthwise-separable adapter offers modest improve-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ments on boundary-sensitive metrics (+1.2 BFScore over LoRA-only), suggesting that high-resolution spatial

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: refinement benefits thin-structure delineation. However, gains are dataset-dependent and may require tuning

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: for optimal integration.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Topology regularization benefits connectivity. Adding clDice loss improves skeleton-based metrics (clDice)

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: by +0.8 points on average, with the effect most pronounced on images with complex vessel branching. How-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 5 Conclusion, Limitations, and Broader Impact

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: We introduced TopoLoRA-SAM, a topology-aware and parameter-efficient adaptation framework for the

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Segment Anything Model (SAM) targeting binary semantic segmentation across diverse domains. Our ap-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: proach combines Low-Rank Adaptation (LoRA) in the frozen ViT encoder, a lightweight spatial convolu

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: tional adapter, and optional topology-aware supervision via differentiable clDice. Across five benchmarks

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: spanning retinal vessels, polyp segmentation, and SAR imagery, TopoLoRA-SAM achieves the best retina-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: average Dice and the best overall average Dice among evaluated methods, while training only 5.2% of

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: model parameters. Notably, on the challenging CHASE_DB1 dataset, our method improves Dice by up to

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: +8.4 points with substantially lower variance, highlighting the robustness of parameter-efficient adaptation.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Topology-focused metrics (clDice and BFScore) further confirm improved connectivity preservation for thin

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: structures.

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: Our ablation studies indicate that LoRA is the primary driver of performance gains, while the spatial adapter

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: and topology-aware loss provide complementary but more sensitive benefits. In particular, topology regular-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: ization depends on careful weighting and does not universally improve cross-dataset generalization. Moreover,

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: while TopoLoRA-SAM trains few parameters, the frozen SAM backbone still incurs non-trivial memory and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: inference costs, which may limit deployment in resource-constrained settings. This work is intended as a

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: research contribution and does not constitute a validated clinical or operational system. We encourage re-

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: sponsible use, especially in medical and remote sensing contexts, and release our codebase and trained models

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: to support reproducibility and further research. Promising future directions include extension to video and

layout_dets.label: ocr_text
layout_dets.text: 3D segmentation, multi-class settings, and domain-adaptive topology regularization
